title: " Correspondances " fonctorielles. Dualité des topos : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: the dossier is about 'functorial correspondences' (profunctors) and a duality for toposes. The page catalogues equivalent ways of encoding a presheaf on a product of small categories, first for two factors, then for any finite family.

Notation (read off the NB):
- A^ = Hom(A°, Ens) is the category of presheaves. A^∨ = Hom(A, Ens) is the category of covariant functors, i.e. presheaves on A°.
- A° sits fully faithfully in two places, A^{∧°} ← A° → A^∨:
  - A^∨ is the free cocompletion of A° (under small colimits);
  - A^{∧°} = (A^)° is the free completion of A° under small limits.
- The decorations on Hom are as follows. Hom_! means functors commuting with small colimits. Hom^! means functors commuting with small limits. Several indices (!!, mixed) mean the condition holds separately in each variable.

Two-variable case.
The centre of the circle is (A×B)^ = Hom(A°×B°, Ens), a profunctor between A and B.

Inner nodes, by currying (two distinct, each drawn twice for symmetry of the quadrants):
- (A×B)^ ≃ Hom(A°, B^) ≃ Hom(B°, A^).

Middle ring, by the universal properties of the two free completions (four nodes):
- Hom(A°, B^) ≃ Hom^!(A^{∧°}, B^) ≃ Hom_!(A^∨, B^);
- symmetrically for B.
- Together with the two inner forms, these are the '6 cas': the source is one of A°, A^{∧°}, A^∨ and the target is B^ (or A ↔ B swapped).

Outer circle: four two-variable 'pairings' A^{∧°} or A^∨ × B^{∧°} or B^∨ → Ens (the '4 cas'), each continuous or cocontinuous separately in each variable:
- Hom^{!!}(A^{∧°}, B^{∧°}; Ens);
- Hom^!_!(A^{∧°}, B^∨; Ens);
- Hom_{!!}(A^∨, B^∨; Ens);
- Hom_!^!(A^∨, B^{∧°}; Ens).

The arrows from the middle ring to the circle are explicit:
- From F: B^{∧°} → A^ (limit-preserving), take (a, b) ↦ Hom_{A^}(a, F b). This preserves limits in a ∈ A^{∧°}, since colimits in A^ are limits in A^{∧°}.
- From G: A^∨ → B^ (colimit-preserving), take (a, b) ↦ G(a) ⊗_B b. Here ⊗_B : B^ × B^∨ → Ens is the coend tensor product, which is cocontinuous in each variable.

The four corner labels (A^→), (B^→), (A^∨→), (B^∨→) mark which completion is being used as the source or target in each quadrant. Altogether there are 1 + 6 + 4 = 11 descriptions. The note says all arrows are equivalences of categories.

General case.
- Data: (A_i)_{i∈I} is a finite family of small categories, with A_{I'} = ∏_{i∈I'} A_i.
- Partition I = ⊔_{j∈J} I_j and the block set J = J^+ ⊔ J^-. Put I^± = ⊔_{j∈J^±} I_j.
- Each block j ∈ J^- is 'dualised' to A_{I_j}^∨ (cocontinuous variable). Each block j ∈ J^+ is dualised to A_{I_j}^{∧°} (continuous variable).
- The claimed equivalences are
  A_I^ ≃ Hom^!_!(∏_{J^-} A^∨_{I_j}, ∏_{J^+} A^{∧°}_{I_j}; Ens)
       ≃ Hom_!(∏_{J^-} A^∨_{I_j}, A_{I^+}^)
       ≃ Hom^!(∏_{J^+} A^{∧°}_{I_j}, A_{I^-}^).
- The two-variable circle is the case I = {1, 2} with singleton blocks.
- Finiteness is assumed 'pour play safe'.

Purpose: to set up a calculus of multi-variable 'correspondances fonctorielles' (multi-profunctors) of mixed variance. This is presumably the groundwork for the announced topos duality, where a topos and its 'dual' play the roles of A^ and A^{∧°} / A^∨.
errors: No mathematical error. All equivalences follow from currying plus the universal properties of free (co)completions. 'Commute with limits' must be read as 'small limits', and multi-variable conditions as holding separately in each variable.
The inner nodes Hom(A°,B^) and Hom(B°,A^) are each drawn twice; this is a symmetry convention, not an error.

Finiteness of I and J is not actually needed, at least for J^- (separately cocontinuous functors on an infinite product still correspond to presheaves on the product). The 'play safe' caution is reasonable for J^+ and for size issues.

ideas.what: Presheaves on A×B ≃ functors A°→B^ ≃ cocontinuous functors from the free cocompletion of A° (= A^∨) to B^ ≃ continuous functors from A^{∧°} to B^
ideas.modern_name: Profunctors/distributors as cocontinuous functors between presheaf categories; free (co)completion universal property
ideas.where_published: SGA4 Exposé I (extension of functors to presheaves, cocontinuous functors on Â); Pursuing Stacks uses A^ notation

ideas.what: Bivariant pairings A^∨×B^∨→Ens cocontinuous in each variable, equivalent to (A×B)^; mixed continuous/cocontinuous variants
ideas.modern_name: Tensor product of cocomplete categories, PSh(A)⊠PSh(B) ≃ PSh(A×B); multi-cocontinuous functors
ideas.usually_credited_to: Kelly (Basic Concepts of Enriched Category Theory, 1982), Day–Street

ideas.what: Mixed-variance multi-variable dictionary: partition the index set into blocks and choose for each block a 'polarity' (∨ = cocontinuous, ∧° = continuous)
ideas.modern_name: Multi-profunctors / polycategorical or Chu-like organisation of presheaf categories; Isbell-duality pair (A^ , A^∨)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Polycategories (Szabo, Lambek); Chu constructions (Barr, Chu 1979); Isbell duality (Isbell 1966)

missed.claim: The page is the combinatorial groundwork for a 'dualité des topos' using signed (±) multi-variable correspondences. The mixed-polarity bookkeeping (J^+/J^-) is a systematic framework that Grothendieck did not develop further in published texts. The individual equivalences are standard.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Only as a historical marker: Grothendieck around 1982 (cf. Pursuing Stacks period) organised profunctor calculus with explicit polarities, close to later Chu/polycategory or 'Isbell duality' viewpoints. The mathematics itself is known.

deep.surprise_reason: Clean, careful organisation of well-known profunctor and free-(co)completion equivalences, including the mixed continuous/cocontinuous polarity bookkeeping. Everything is standard (Bénabou, Kelly, Day–Street); the only mildly interesting element is the signed multi-block generalisation as a prelude to a topos duality.
transcription_corrections: The circle has 4 outer nodes, 4 middle-ring nodes and 4 inner nodes. The inner nodes are Hom(B°,A^) and Hom(A°,B^), each appearing twice, from upper-left/lower-right and upper-right/lower-left of the centre.
Top-right header: the sources A°, A^{∧°}, A^∨ (resp. B°, B^{∧°}, B^∨) map to the targets B^ (resp. A^), hence '6 cas'. The second line is |A^{∧°} ou A^∨| × |B^{∧°} ou B^∨| → Ens, '4 cas'.
Right-margin note: 'toutes les flèches du diagramme sont des équivalences de catégories'.
Bottom margin note: 'je suppose I, J finis pour "play safe"'.
